title: Gaussian generator integration by parts
statement: Let $n\ge0$ and let $\gamma_n$ be the product of $n$ standard Gaussian measures on $\mathbb R^n$. Suppose $f,g,u,v:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ are such that $u$ is the Gaussian generator of $f$ and $v$ is the Gaussian generator of $g$, and suppose $f$ and $g$ are three times continuously differentiable. Then the function $x\mapsto\sum_{i=1}^n \partial_i f(x)\,\partial_i g(x)$ is integrable with respect to $\gamma_n$, and $\int f v\,d\gamma_n=\int\sum_{i=1}^n\partial_i f\,\partial_i g\,d\gamma_n$.
